chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who pledged a security deposit for an unspecified time, then he was absent. Is there a time for him that he sells his security? He said: No, until its owner comes.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a pledged item if the debtor is absent and the time is unspecified?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedure for liquidating a mortgage (rahn) when the repayment term is indefinite and the debtor is absent, ruling that the creditor must wait for the debtor's return before selling the pledged asset. This ensures fairness by preventing premature disposal of the collateral, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the debtor's rights in ambiguous contractual terms. The ruling underscores the principle that uncertainty in timing does not grant the creditor immediate unilateral power to liquidate without due process.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyr Bin Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who held a security deposit as mortgage to an unspecified time, then he was absent. Is there a time for him that he sells his security?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until its owner comes over’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who held al-Rahn (security-deposit) for an unspecified time and his party disappeared; if he had a time limit within which he could sell al-Rahn (security deposit). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, until his party comes.’”
